business_problem: ALTR needed to help customers unlock cloud data securely across regions while keeping governance and observability strong and avoiding the cost growth that often comes with global expansion.
solution_summary: ALTR built its automated data access and security platform on AWS and then shifted the solution to a serverless architecture so it could expand globally without a matching rise in infrastructure cost. Amazon API Gateway provides the managed API front door for the service, AWS Lambda runs event-driven application logic and security workflows, and Amazon Neptune stores metadata that ALTR uses to make governance decisions quickly. The platform monitors customer data environments so users can create access policies, classify data, run observability analyses, and protect sensitive information with tokenization, while Snowflake acts as a connected warehouse in the broader solution. Because the design is serverless, ALTR can concentrate on software and policy controls rather than patching virtual servers, making it easier to add regions, streamline security checks, and offer highly available service at competitive pricing.

solution_components.name: Amazon API Gateway
solution_components.role: Provides the scalable API layer for ALTR's automated data-security service.

solution_components.name: AWS Lambda
solution_components.role: Runs event-driven security, notification, and lifecycle checks in the serverless platform.

solution_components.name: Amazon Neptune
solution_components.role: Stores metadata used to make governance decisions quickly inside the platform.

data_flow: Customer cloud-data activity is monitored by ALTR's service, policy and security requests enter through Amazon API Gateway, AWS Lambda processes events and enforcement logic, and metadata in Amazon Neptune is used to evaluate governance decisions and observability outcomes.
business_outcome: ALTR more than doubled its annual recurring revenue and customer count, grew Snowflake-based annual recurring revenue by more than 472 percent, expanded into new regions, and increased AWS production expenses by only 2.4 percent while keeping the service scalable and highly available.
